Project has been publicly postponed by the project sponsors, possibly indefinitely, but could be reinitiated later. A project can enter this status at On Hold any point in the development process. Project has initiated the early project development process. This step details the need for a facility, involved parties, regulatory agencies, existing Pre-filing work, and a public participation plan and is usually initiated 7–8 months before the application process begins. Project has initiated a formal application with the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC). FERC prepares an Environmental Impact Applied Statement (EIS) after conferring with concerned organizations and the public to determine necessity, safety, and feasibility of a project. Regulatory approval is based upon the final EIS. Project has received a permit to construct and operate, usually accommodated to any conditions that must be met and the market rate authority. Approved From this point, the project must still obtain Clean Air and Water Act permits and state approval; these permits are often pursued concurrently with the FERC permit process but are also contingent upon the EIS. Project has commenced actual construction; site preparation does not qualify. Facility must file monthly reports offering an activity summary, Under Construction outstanding permit status, current project schedule, and compliance with environmental conditions outlined in the approval document. Completed Project has reached commercial operation.
